summary: The note describes the Diet of Worms of 1521, an imperial diet (formal assembly of the whole Holy Roman Empire) held at the Heylshof Garden in the Imperial Free City of Worms. It is best remembered for the Edict of Worms, which addressed Martin Luther and the effects of the Protestant Reformation. The diet ran from 28 January to 26 May 1521 under the presidency of Emperor Charles V.
one_line: The 1521 imperial diet at Worms, remembered for the Edict of Worms addressing Martin Luther and the Protestant Reformation.
key_facts: The Diet of Worms 1521 was an imperial diet (assembly) of the Holy Roman Empire.
The Diet of Worms was held at the Heylshof Garden in Worms.
In 1521, Worms was an Imperial Free City of the Empire.
An imperial diet was a formal deliberative assembly of the whole Empire.
The Diet of Worms is most memorable for the Edict of Worms (Wormser Edikt).
The Edict of Worms addressed Martin Luther and the effects of the Protestant Reformation.
The Diet of Worms was conducted from 28 January to 26 May 1521.
The Emperor Charles V presided over the Diet of Worms.
The German name of the event is Reichstag zu Worms.
